topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: On "Black Sunday" during this period, so-called "black blizzards" swept through the plains states.
question.text: "Okies" migrated west during what period of severe drought and agriculture damage in the 1930s?
question.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about famous American criminals.
swap.text: This criminal was able to break out of what was said to be an "escape-proof" jail in 1934. He and his namesake gang terrorized the Midwest, allegedly robbing 24 banks and four police stations.
swap.clue: Harold Cassidy and Wilhelm Loeser operated on this man and Homer Van Meter to change their appearance and fingerprints, which helped Jay Robert Nash claim that Jimmy Lawrence died after this man met with Polly Hamilton and Anna Sage.

question.text: The Microsoft lawsuit claimed it abused this economic status of being the only seller in its market and destroying competition.
question.clue: Lizzie Magie developed the predecessor to this product in the Georgist community of Arden, Delaware. Charles Darrow was long credited as the inventor of this consumer product.

swap.leadin: In Schechter Poultry Corporation v. United States, known as the "sick chicken case," the Supreme Court unanimously decided that this law was unconstitutional.
swap.text: Name this piece of legislation, signed in 1933, that established the National Recovery Administration, known for its Blue Eagle emblem, and the Public Works Administration, which survived the Supreme Court's ruling in Schechter.
swap.clue: It set up an agency headed by General Hugh S. Johnson that, and it reduced maximum hours so that more people couple be employed, while its Section 7a was an important concession to labor unions.

question.leadin: Douglas MacArthur used army infantry to help the police disperse this group.
question.text: Identify this group of army veterans which marched on Washington in 1932 to demand redemption of their service certificates from World War I.
question.clue: It protested a bill that was proposed by Wright Patman by embarking on a "death march" to Capitol Hill.

swap.leadin: Businesses that supported this organization displayed a poster of a blue eagle holding a gear and lightning bolts.
swap.text: Name this New Deal agency forced to cease operations after its founding legislation was ruled unconstitutional in Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States.
swap.clue: This New Deal agency was declared unconstitutional in the Schechter Poultry case. It included various labor provisions such as minimum wages, and companies supporting it placed a blue eagle sign by their stores.

question.leadin: Answer the following about activities on our home front during World War I.
question.text: During the war, this man ran the U.S. Food Administration and encouraged voluntary rationing at home. Later, as President, he got saddled with the stock market crash.
question.clue: He was appointed head of food distribution in West Germany after WWII due to his successful heading of the US Food Administration after WWI.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Francis Townsend.
swap.text: Later on, Townsend created the Union Party along with Gerald L. K. Smith and this Detroit-based Catholic priest. This priest used his radio program and newspaper, Social Justice, to spread his antisemitic views.
swap.clue: This man established the National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica in Royal Oak, Michigan.

question.leadin: An entire floor of IBM machines in Baltimore's Candler Building was devoted to handling paperwork from this program.
question.text: Name this program begun during the New Deal. Alan Greenspan headed a commission that increased contributions to this program's Trust Fund.
question.answerHtml: Social Security [accept OAI or Old-Age Insurance Program; or Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance; or OASDI]
question.clue: The Supreme Court case Flemming v. Nestor established that Congress can revise and amend this policy, which was expanded to include disability in 1954.

swap.leadin: This man pushed for the popularization of radio as secretary of commerce, in which capacity he also vastly expand the department by siphoning off poorly managed duties from other agencies.
swap.text: Name this man whose response to the Great Mississippi Flood helped propel him to the presidency, an engineer who saved millions of Europeans from starvation during World War I.
swap.clue: A baby was among the dead after this president ordered a force led by Walter Waters to leave the Anacostia Flats; that Bonus Army was dispersed by Douglas MacArthur.

question.text: This physician developed a plan for state-funded old-age pensions as a way to stimulate economic spending during the Depression. While FDR eventually adopted the Social Security Act, this man was not pleased with the conservative changes the President made to his proposal.
question.clue: This doctor, another critic of FDR's New Deal, popularized a namesake national pension plan which influenced the Social Security Act.

swap.leadin: This politician campaigned for governor with the slogan "Every man a king, but no one wears a crown."
swap.text: Name this Louisiana politician, nicknamed "The Kingfish," who proposed the "Share Our Wealth" program as a senator. This politician was assassinated by Carl Weiss just prior to a likely run in the 1936 presidential election.
swap.clue: This author of My First Days in the White House ousted Benjamin Pavy from office, leading this governor to be assassinated by dentist Carl Weiss in 1935.

question.leadin: During a visit to China, this man was infatuated by Soong Mei-Ling and may have had an affair with her.
question.text: Name this man who, as a representative for the utility corporation C&S, spent 7 years arguing against the TVA. This man unsuccessfully ran for president against FDR in 1940.
question.clue: This lawyer and corporate president of Commonwealth and Southern Corporation who was the Republican candidate for President in 1940.

swap.text: Gangster Ciro Terranova's monopoly on artichokes led this politician to ban them in 1935. This politician sought to curb racketeering by smashing a pinball machine with a sledgehammer as a media stunt.
swap.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

question.text: While the theory did not really take off until the 1960s and beyond, several theorists claimed this person and partner Fred Noonan were either executed by the Japanese or forced to work for them, perhaps as one of the people using the name "Tokyo Rose."
question.clue: One theory surrounding the whereabouts of this person and their companion, Fred Noonan, was that they were executed by Japanese soldiers on Saipan.

swap.text: Late in her life, Lucy Parsons also assisted in the defense of this group, who were accused of raping two white women on a train. They were exonerated in the 1932 case Powell v. Alabama.
swap.clue: James Horton presided over a trial of this group for the "god fearing people of Decatur County;" in that trial, Samuel Leibowitz defended them for the American Communist Party.

question.leadin: Lyndon Johnson's big break as a politician came when he was appointed head of the Texas division of this agency, which was headed by Aubrey Willis Williams.
question.text: Name this New Deal agency that paid boys and girls between the ages of 16 and 25 anywhere from $6 to $40 per hour for work study projects.

swap.leadin: During a vote on Charles Warren's nomination for attorney general, this man made a mad dash across Washington in a taxi cab to break the tie, becoming the subject of a parody of "Paul Revere's Ride."
swap.text: Name this vice president, the devisor of a namesake plan following WWI, whose scathing inaugural speech against the rules of the Senate was one of the many reasons that his superior, Calvin Coolidge, hated him.
swap.clue: This U.S. Vice President who was succeeded in that position in 1929 by Charles Curtis.

question.leadin: Answer some stuff about the history of the UAW.
question.text: Reuther and Richard Frankensteen were attacked by men hired by Ford internal security executive Harry Bennett during a leaflet campaign in this 1937 incident at the River Rouge complex. This so-called "battle" is named for the location where Reuther posed to take a picture when he was attacked.
question.clue: This incident in which security guards under Harry Bennett started beating up Richard Frankensteen and Walter Reuther during a photoshoot at the River Rouge Ford Motor complex.

swap.text: This FDR advisor ran the Works Progress Administration. Before American entrance into World War II, he coordinated unofficial negotiations with Winston Churchill.
swap.clue: The phrase "Arsenal of Democracy" was suggested by this advisor to FDR, who crafted the WPA and was integral in implementing the Lend Lease Program.
